description: One cause named for a move that plainly had several.
A relative claim ('hit hardest', 'outperformed') with nothing to compare against.
A percentage asserted rather than measured, or materially off the tape.
The news landed near the move in time, not behind it in mechanism.
SQ, index rebalance, ex-dividend, futures roll, buyback or margin-tape effects unconsidered.
A single-name move blamed on a sector-wide cause, or a sector move read off one name.
Written as though it was knowable in advance; the story fits because the outcome is known.
The transmission channel cited has since decayed, and is still being cited.
Confidence carries no information — every claim lands in the same narrow band.
The observation conveniently argues for an open position, or rationalises a loss.
Restates the 07:00 brief's own channel as an independent observation.
A causal claim with no source behind it at all.
Argues the opposite of a recent observation over the same names, without acknowledging it.
Nothing about the claim could have turned out false.
